memories.memory_text: I heard that the service was kept small, probably because of recent losses in the pack, and I figured there'd be a reception afterward where I might stay late to help out.

grounded_facts: Adrian Keaton recognizes Valerie Whitaker in the back seat, now bearing the appearance of a werewolf, confirming his recent transformation.
memories.memory_text: I saw Adrian Keaton recognize Valerie Whitaker in the back seat, and when she asked him if he had transformed too, he confirmed it with that aggressive tone he now carries.

grounded_facts: Noel Calloway arrives in his Rabbit with Bennett Arden and Valerie Whitaker, the latter having transformed into a werewolf, indicating his inclusion in the pack.
memories.memory_text: I drove my Rabbit to Silverbrook School with Bennett Arden and Valerie Whitaker, and once we arrived, I got out and let Bennett Arden take over driving so I could talk to her.

grounded_facts: Noel Calloway delays attending the funeral to speak with Adrian Keaton first, signaling urgency in their interaction.
memories.memory_text: I made sure to tell the guys to go on to the funeral without me because I had to speak with Adrian Keaton first—there wasn't time to wait.

grounded_facts: Noel Calloway questions Adrian Keaton about how many Silverline Council are present and for how long, showing hostility.
memories.memory_text: I asked Adrian Keaton how many Silverline Council were there and how long they were staying, because I needed to know what we were dealing with.

grounded_facts: Adrian Keaton sarcastically tells Noel Calloway to report back to Emery Winslow, implying he's acting like a subordinate.
memories.memory_text: I heard Adrian Keaton tell me sarcastically to report back to Emery Winslow, as if I were just following orders.

grounded_facts: Noel Calloway acknowledges that he has hurt Adrian Keaton again, breaking his own promise.
memories.memory_text: I realized I've hurt Adrian Keaton again and admitted to her that I keep breaking my promise not to cause her pain.

grounded_facts: Noel Calloway presses his hand to Adrian Keaton's cheek, expressing emotional vulnerability and care.
memories.memory_text: I pressed my hand to Adrian Keaton's cheek, showing her how much I care and letting her see my vulnerability.

grounded_facts: Noel Calloway comes to Silverbrook School during the day, leading to an emotionally charged encounter.
memories.memory_text: I came to Silverbrook School during the day, and I remember the tension between us building as I turned to leave, then seeing the hurt in her eyes—she missed me, and I almost kissed her.

grounded_facts: Noel Calloway and Adrian Keaton nearly kiss, but the moment is interrupted by a the wooden key call.
memories.memory_text: I turned to leave, but when I saw the hurt in her eyes, I couldn't go—I moved back, looked into her eyes, and touched her cheek. I started leaning in to kiss her, and she didn't pull away; we were just a breath apart when the the wooden key rang and shattered the moment.

grounded_facts: Noel Calloway answers the the wooden key and states that someone is at a funeral, then the call ends abruptly.
memories.memory_text: I answered the the wooden key without breaking eye contact with her and said, 'He's not here. He's at a funeral...'—then the line went dead.

grounded_facts: Noel Calloway receives a the wooden key call from Dr. Jordan Arden and reacts with hostility, calling him a 'filthy bloodsucker'.
memories.memory_text: I hung up the the wooden key and called Dr. Jordan Arden a filthy bloodsucker, showing how I really feel about him.

grounded_facts: Noel Calloway dismisses Adrian Keaton's desire to speak to Jordan Arden, showing control over information and tension in their relationship.
memories.memory_text: I dismissed Adrian Keaton's request to speak to Jordan Arden, telling her he didn't ask for her, because I needed to keep control of the situation between us.

grounded_facts: Taylor Brooks appears at the doorway, emotionally devastated, and reveals she has seen a vision of Avery Hale believing Adrian Keaton is dead.
memories.memory_text: I saw Taylor Brooks appear in the doorway, looking completely broken, and I could feel my body reacting—trembling like I might shift any second.

grounded_facts: Taylor Brooks delivers the distressing news that Avery Hale believes Adrian Keaton is dead and is going to the Eastwood Police.
memories.memory_text: I heard Taylor Brooks tell Adrian Keaton that Avery Hale saw a vision where she was dead and that he's on his way to the Eastwood Police in Italy.

grounded_facts: Noel Calloway challenges Adrian Keaton's motivation to go to Avery Hale, reminding her that he abandoned her.
memories.memory_text: I reminded Adrian Keaton that Avery Hale left her behind and didn't want her anymore, trying to make her see that rushing back to him doesn't make sense.

grounded_facts: Adrian Keaton decides to travel to Italy to prove her survival to Avery Hale, preventing him from committing suicide out of guilt.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Adrian Keaton has to go to Italy because Avery Hale won't believe she's alive unless he sees her, and she doesn't want him to kill himself out of guilt.

grounded_facts: Adrian Keaton urgently packs to leave Forks for Italy, prompted by the need to stop Avery Hale from killing himself.
memories.memory_text: I saw Adrian Keaton race into the house and start shoving clothes into a bag, and even when I tried to stop her, she pulled away and said she was legally free to go and would leave a note.

grounded_facts: Taylor Brooks arrives with airline tickets, enabling Adrian Keaton's trip to Italy.
memories.memory_text: I saw Taylor Brooks come in and say she had the airline tickets, which meant Adrian Keaton could go to Italy.

grounded_facts: Noel Calloway accuses Taylor Brooks of recklessly delivering Adrian Keaton to the Eastwood Police, comparing it to offering her as a gift.
memories.memory_text: I told Taylor Brooks that the Eastwood Police in Italy aren't like the Silverline Council—they're monsters, and bringing Adrian Keaton to them is like offering her as a gift.

grounded_facts: Adrian Keaton physically intervenes to prevent Noel Calloway from morphing and attacking Taylor Brooks.
memories.memory_text: I was about to shift and attack Taylor Brooks when Adrian Keaton stepped in and stopped me by grabbing Taylor Brooks, preventing me from morphing.

grounded_facts: Noel Calloway physically stops Adrian Keaton by grabbing her arm and emotionally urges her to stay for Tristan Hayes and for himself.
memories.memory_text: I grabbed Adrian Keaton's arm and pleaded with her to stay, saying please for Tristan Hayes and for me.

grounded_facts: Adrian Keaton hugs Noel Calloway and says a final goodbye, recognizing it may be the last time she sees him.
memories.memory_text: I saw the love in my eyes reflected in hers when she hugged me, and I knew this could be the last time I ever see her as she pulled away and said, 'Bye, Noel Calloway.'

grounded_facts: Adrian Keaton makes the decision to depart from her house despite Noel Calloway's plea, indicating a finality in her choice.
memories.memory_text: I watched, agonized, as she ran to her car and drove away, knowing she had made her final choice to leave despite my plea.

grounded_facts: Taylor Brooks tells Adrian Keaton that the Eastwood Police may see them as threats and could kill them both.
memories.memory_text: I heard Taylor Brooks tell Adrian Keaton that the Eastwood Police might see them as threats and could kill them both.

grounded_facts: Adrian Keaton refuses to be dissuaded from staying with the Silverline Council, even after Taylor Brooks warns her about the Eastwood Police threat.
memories.memory_text: I saw Adrian Keaton refuse to be dissuaded from staying with the Silverline Council, even after Taylor Brooks warned her about the Eastwood Police threat.

grounded_facts: A wolf, implied to be Noel Calloway, is seen retreating into the Fairview Park, leaving behind shredded clothing.
memories.memory_text: I remember retreating into the Fairview Park on all fours, leaving behind the tattered remains of my clothes—I knew I had to get away after Adrian Keaton made her choice.

grounded_facts: Noel Calloway suddenly appears in front of Avery Hale's moving car, forcing Avery Hale to brake abruptly, then walks away into Northbridge Plaza.
memories.memory_text: I stepped into the road right in front of Avery Hale's moving car, making him slam on the brakes, then I turned and walked into Northbridge Plaza.

grounded_facts: Adrian Keaton forcefully leaves the car after Noel Calloway's appearance, intending to confront him first.
memories.memory_text: I think Adrian Keaton got out of the car right after I walked away, probably to come after me, though I didn't see her do it.

grounded_facts: Avery Hale expresses gratitude to Noel Calloway for keeping Adrian Keaton alive during his absence.
memories.memory_text: Avery Hale told me he was thanking me for keeping Adrian Keaton alive when he was gone, but I wasn't sure if he meant it or if it was just another move in his game.

grounded_facts: Avery Hale declares he will not leave Adrian Keaton's side unless she tells him to.
memories.memory_text: I heard Avery Hale say he wouldn't leave Adrian Keaton's side unless she told him to, and it only confirmed how determined he was to keep her close.

grounded_facts: Noel Calloway reminds Avery Hale of the treaty clause: any Cullen biting a human breaks the truce.
memories.memory_text: I reminded Avery Hale about the treaty—we both know that if any of them bites a human, the truce is over. I made sure he understood it was non-negotiable.

grounded_facts: Noel Calloway warns Adrian Keaton that the pack will kill her if she becomes a vampire.
memories.memory_text: I told Adrian Keaton I wouldn't let her become one of them—she's not going to turn into a vampire, not if I can stop it.

grounded_facts: Overcome with rage and pain, Noel Calloway transforms into a wolf mid-air after being pushed by Avery Hale.
memories.memory_text: I was so overcome with rage and pain that when Avery Hale pushed me, I transformed into a wolf mid-air.

grounded_facts: Adrian Keaton steps between Avery Hale and Noel Calloway, threatening to make them go through her if they fight.
memories.memory_text: I saw Adrian Keaton step right between me and Avery Hale, and she said, 'You do this, you'll be going through me,' making it clear she'd block any attack from either of us.

grounded_facts: Avery Hale reads Noel Calloway's thoughts, provoking an aggressive reaction.
memories.memory_text: I saw Avery Hale look into my mind, asking Adrian Keaton if I was going to hurt him, and that made me furious—he had no right to invade my thoughts like that.

grounded_facts: Adrian Keaton tells Noel Calloway that she loves him but would still choose Avery Hale.
Adrian Keaton tells Noel Calloway she loves him but cannot change her feelings for Avery Hale, admitting she would choose Avery Hale.
memories.memory_text: I heard Adrian Keaton tell me she loves me, but she also said she would always choose Avery Hale, that it's always been him.

grounded_facts: A tense meeting in Northbridge Plaza between Avery Hale, Adrian Keaton, and Noel Calloway, where unresolved tensions over Adrian Keaton's future and the treaty come to a head.
memories.memory_text: I stood in Northbridge Plaza, arms folded, watching Avery Hale and Adrian Keaton approach, and I could feel the tension building between us as Adrian Keaton stepped in front of me, trying to calm things down before I finally bolted away.

grounded_facts: Adrian Keaton asserts her right to choose vampirism, knowing it will break the treaty and endanger her relationship with Noel Calloway.
memories.memory_text: I saw Adrian Keaton stand up and declare she’d go through with it, knowing full well it would break the treaty and put her in danger—not just from the Eastwood Police, but from me and my pack.

grounded_facts: After Adrian Keaton's confession, Noel Calloway bolts from the scene, howling in pain.
memories.memory_text: After she said it, I couldn't stay—I bolted into the Fairview Park and howled in pain, unable to hold back the agony.

memories.memory_text: I saw Avery Hale step into the sunlight, and his skin shattered the light into a thousand rainbow shards, like he was made of diamonds—I couldn't look away, even though I was terrified someone would see.
I reached out to my grandmother, only to touch glass—my heart stopped when I realized the old woman in the mirror was me, aged and wrinkled, staring back in horror.
I told him I needed forever — that being human meant losing him eventually, no matter what. I reached for his hand, but he pulled away.
I asked for a kiss — one last thing on my birthday — and when he kissed me, it started soft but turned desperate, like he was saying goodbye. Then he just left.
He said he didn't want me — those words hit like a slap, and I stepped back, trying to make sense of how someone who held me so closely could suddenly look at me with nothing in his eyes.

He asked me not to do anything stupid — for Tristan Hayes's sake — and something in the way he said it made me feel like he was already gone, like he was giving me instructions from a distance I couldn't cross.

I remember the slam of my the black radio door when Tristan Hayes blocked me—his face was tight with fear, not anger—and then he said I had to leave Forks, go to my mom. I just said, 'I'm not leaving Forks,' like that could stop him.

I was running through the trees, heart pounding, desperate to find him—then I saw Avery Hale, just a few yards away, but his face was so cold. When I stepped toward him, he bolted, and no matter how fast I tried to follow, he kept disappearing further into the dark until he was gone.
I barely recognized Bennett Arden—his hair was gone, his body stronger, his easy smile replaced by something blank and serious. He looked like one of them now, not the boy I used to know.
Emery Winslow turned and looked right at me before he jumped—like he was challenging me, or warning me. I couldn’t look away until he cut into the water.

I felt the the old box lurch forward, my hands shaking on the clutch, and then Avery Hale was there—his voice sharp in my head, telling me to stop—but I didn’t. I kept going, faster, until the wind ripped through my hair and for one second, I wasn’t broken, I wasn’t haunted—I was free.

Noel Calloway’s hand was hot on the the old box as he lifted it off me, too hot—unnaturally so—and when I looked at him, his face was tight with something I couldn’t name, something raw and close to pain, like he was holding back more than just frustration.

I sat there, restless, while Tristan Hayes watched his game—my fingers hovered over the the wooden key, heart pounding, before I finally left that message for Noel Calloway, my voice unsteady as I apologized for everything I felt and hoped he’d get better soon.

I saw the empty space where Avery Hale’s car used to be, and everyone else was with someone—couples everywhere—so I just kept my head down and walked faster, but then I called out to Noel Calloway’s the black radio, voice cracking—‘Hi Noel Calloway. Your Tristan Hayes said you have mono. He won’t let me visit but… would you call me?’
I kept staring at the the wooden key, willing it to ring, my fingers twitching at the thought of calling him again—I just needed to hear his voice, even if I didn’t say anything real.

I pressed the the wooden key to my ear, voice shaking as I left another message—'Noel Calloway. Please. Call me.' My forehead rested against the cold receiver, the silence on the other end crushing me.

I saw Kendall Huxley step out of the trees, and for a second I thought—maybe this meant Avery Hale was near, maybe he sent him. But then he started circling me, asking about the Silverline Council, and I could feel the way his voice changed, like he wasn't here to help at all.
Avery Hale’s voice told me to lie, to say they visited all the time—but when Kendall Huxley kept pressing, the air turned sharp with danger, and I knew he wasn’t going to let me walk away.

I knocked on the door, and Bennett Bennett said Noel Calloway was out with friends—but I knew something was wrong. He wouldn’t let me in, not even when I mentioned the mono story he’d told my Tristan Hayes.

I turned toward the knock and saw Noel Calloway—his face was so different, his hair cut short, his eyes cold and hard, nothing like the Noel Calloway I knew. I froze, stunned, before stepping out of the the black radio to face him.

I reached for Noel Calloway’s arm, stunned—he moved differently, sure-footed, like he’d shed the awkwardness overnight, and when I asked what happened to him, his face was hard, closed off, like he didn’t even recognize me anymore.

I asked him what happened, if I could help, and if Emery Winslow had done something to him. He said Emery Winslow was trying to help and blamed the Silverline Council. When I said they were gone, he told me he couldn't be friends with me anymore. I begged him, but he cut me off, said it was over, that I'd already lost him, told me to go home and not come back, then ran inside.

I woke up thinking it was just another dream, but then I heard that screeching again—fingernails dragging against the glass. My heart slammed into my chest as I scrambled for something, anything, to defend myself.
I told Noel Calloway to show me the truth — I didn't care about the danger anymore. I'd take the risk if it meant understanding his pain.
I stopped him from leaving and then he pulled me into a hug — my cheek pressed against his chest, warm and solid — and for a moment, I just held on, feeling how much he was hurting.
I had to know why—if I was going to lose someone else, I couldn’t just wait. I turned off the road and drove into the Fairview Park, tires crunching over broken branches in the dark.

I saw the scar on Graham Dalton's face—three red lines pulling down her eye and twisting her mouth—and when she said, 'So you're the vampire girl,' I knew everything had changed. Werewolves were real, and I was standing in the middle of their world.

Noel Calloway didn't say a word, but when our eyes met, he gave me that slow, serious nod toward the door—our signal. I knew then we had things to talk about, things he couldn't say in front of the others.
I thought Noel Calloway was talking about killing hikers, and I was horrified—until he said the only thing they kill is vampires. It hit me like a shock: they’re not monsters, they’re protectors.

When Noel Calloway mentioned Quinn Colter would keep coming back, I froze—then it clicked. She’s not after the tribe or random people. She’s hunting me. I could see it in his face when he realized it too.

I walked in and saw them all together, the house warm and alive, and for a second I felt like I was home — I said, 'You're here,' but no one looked at me, and then Avery Hale yanked me away and threw me out.
I looked into Noel Calloway's eyes and told him I wouldn't let him disappear — for a second, I almost kissed him, but I pulled away.
I saw Jordan Arden's car in the driveway and shouted for Noel Calloway to stop — I opened the door while the the black radio was moving and jumped out, even though he tried to keep me inside.

Shawn Dalton’s eyes locked on mine as he told me to go make my preparations — his voice was smooth, but the weight of what he meant pressed down on me, and I could feel Quinn Delaney’s glare like a blade as I moved toward Avery Hale.
I stood in front of the Silverline Council and asked them to vote on whether I should become one of them — my voice was steady, but my hands wouldn’t stop trembling.
Avery Hale didn’t say another word — he just got up and slammed the door behind him, and I felt it like a punch, but I couldn’t let myself react.

dialogue_exemplars: He wasn't real. I knew that. I didn't care. I needed to see him. If danger's what it took, that's what I'd find.
I can help you with it -- but first -- (pulling out her camera) I need a picture. My mom's expecting a the blue photograph full of memories.
They'll come after your whole family. You'd risk that just to keep me human?
Avery Hale took everything with him. Including my life. He promised it would be like he never existed......
Time passes. Every tick that goes by... aches...

If I didn't become a vampire, the
Eastwood Police would kill me. If I did, my
best friend would do the job himself,
or get killed in the attempt.
However this turns out, I'm not letting the Eastwood Police hurt you. I'll go back to Italy alone --
But the pain is my only reminder that he was real... that they all were...
You can't protect me from everything - something's going to separate us -- accident, illness, old age... as long as I'm human...
No, please -- I want you to seriously think about this. If I join you, you'll be stuck with me for a long time - forever. It's a huge decision. And I want - I need your honesty here.
Then take my soul. I don't care! I don't want it without you --

relations.relation_summary: Avery Hale and Adrian Keaton share a deeply intense romantic relationship characterized by profound emotional intimacy, physical affection, and mutual devotion, as consistently evidenced by their tender interactions—kissing, embracing, holding hands, and exchanging loving gazes—across multiple contexts. Avery Hale consistently assumes the role of protector, repeatedly placing himself between Adrian Keaton and danger, whether from the Silverline Council, Sasha Vaughn, or the Eastwood Police, and even shielding her from Shawn Dalton's psychic intrusion. His protective behavior is rooted in deep emotional investment, demonstrated when he admits considering suicide after Adrian Keaton was endangered by Bennett Langley, underscoring how her safety is tied to his emotional survival. Adrian Keaton, in turn, exhibits equal devotion by intervening to stop Avery Hale from self-destructive actions, such as when she physically stops him from exposing himself to sunlight, revealing that she protects him emotionally and physically. Their relationship evolves through cycles of separation and reunion: Avery Hale ends their relationship out of protective concern, causing emotional devastation for both, yet Adrian Keaton actively pursues him, showing unwavering commitment. Key events like lying together in the grass, sharing passionate kisses, fleeing danger together, and reaffirming eternal presence highlight their bond's resilience. Despite moments of hostility, distrust, and reluctant separation—driven by Avery Hale’s fear of harming Adrian Keaton—their connection remains central to both characters’ identities and decisions. The narrative arc shows a shift from one-sided protection to mutual care, where Adrian Keaton is not merely protected but also becomes Avery Hale’s emotional anchor, transforming their dynamic into one of reciprocal dependence and shared strength. The evidence confirms a romantic, emotionally charged, and evolving relationship defined by sacrifice, loyalty, and enduring love.

The relationship between Adrian Keaton and Noel Calloway is complex, emotionally charged, and evolves significantly throughout their interactions. Social relationship evidence reveals a deep and multifaceted bond characterized by strong mutual affection, emotional dependency, and recurring conflict. Noel Calloway consistently assumes the role of protector, repeatedly saving Adrian Keaton from physical danger—such as rescuing her from drowning, shielding her from Kendall Huxley, and positioning himself between her and aggressive pack members—demonstrating a protective companion dynamic. Adrian Keaton, in turn, acknowledges Noel Calloway as her emotional anchor, stating he 'has been keeping me afloat' during Avery Hale’s absence, highlighting his role as a supportive companion. Their bond is reinforced through shared activities like repairing and riding motorcycles, which establishes them as collaborators and friends with common interests. These joint efforts foster intimacy, playful banter, and emotional restoration, with Noel Calloway’s cheerful presence lifting Adrian Keaton’s spirits and revitalizing her emotionally. Physical closeness—such as hugging, arm-grabbing, and Noel Calloway pressing his hand to her cheek—along with near-kiss moments and romantic tension, suggest an underlying emotional partnership that transcends mere friendship, despite Adrian Keaton’s repeated insistence they are 'just friends' and her declaration of Noel Calloway as her 'best friend'. However, this closeness is frequently disrupted by hostility. Noel Calloway exhibits resentment and brooding anger, especially when Adrian Keaton prioritizes Avery Hale or chooses to become a vampire, leading to confrontational conflicts over autonomy and emotional betrayal. Adrian Keaton also displays hostility, pushing Noel Calloway away and accusing him of worsening their situation, culminating in Noel Calloway ending their friendship and threatening to oppose her transformation. Key events, such as Adrian Keaton intervening to stop Noel Calloway from morphing, both apologizing after emotional breakdowns, and comforting each other during distress, illustrate mutual care and emotional reciprocity. The relationship evolves from casual friendship into a profound emotional alliance, then fractures under the weight of incompatible loyalties and existential choices. Ultimately, their bond is defined by intense emotional support, protective instincts, collaborative intimacy, and irreconcilable conflict driven by love, loyalty, and divergent paths.

The relationship between Adrian Keaton and Shawn Dalton is defined by a pronounced power imbalance and mutual hostility, underscored by Shawn Dalton's fascination with Adrian Keaton's unique abilities. Social relationship evidence reveals that Shawn Dalton sees potential in Adrian Keaton due to her mental 'gifts'—specifically her immunity to psychic powers—which he views as valuable for the Eastwood Police's interests. However, this fascination coexists with hostility, as Shawn Dalton assesses Adrian Keaton as a potential threat to vampire secrecy, justifying his readiness to eliminate her. This dual perception is mirrored in Adrian Keaton's actions: she repeatedly pleads with Shawn Dalton to stop the violence, even offering her life to protect Avery Hale, but her appeals are met with indifference, illustrating her subordinate position. Key events highlight this dynamic—Shawn Dalton initiates physical contact by reaching for Adrian Keaton’s hand, laughs at her reluctance, and ultimately releases her after contemplation, signaling his control over the interaction. He later informs her that her transformation into an immortal would make her 'intriguing,' reinforcing his objectifying yet captivated stance. Meanwhile, Adrian Keaton’s desperate plea to be killed to spare others underscores her perception of Shawn Dalton as both executioner and ultimate authority. Shawn Dalton consistently disregards her emotional appeals, choosing instead to focus on Avery Hale, further emphasizing Adrian Keaton’s lack of agency in their encounters. The relationship does not evolve toward empathy or alliance; rather, it remains static in its asymmetry, with Shawn Dalton maintaining dominance and Adrian Keaton positioned as a supplicant resisting coercion. The emotional dynamic is tense and adversarial, shaped by Shawn Dalton’s calculated curiosity and Adrian Keaton’s fear-driven resistance.

memories.memory_text: I stepped into the sunlight and let it shine on my skin, knowing Adrian Keaton would see me. I smiled as it sparkled.
I took her aged, wrinkled hand in mine, kissed it, and leaned close to whisper 'Happy birthday'—feeling the fragile warmth of her skin, the weight of time she’d carried without me.

I remember running my hand over the horseshoe scar on Adrian Keaton's arm, feeling the weight of that moment when Bennett Langley had her — I didn't know if I'd find her in time, and the thought of losing her made me consider ending it all.

I told her I had a plan — if she'd died, I would have gone to Italy and provoked the Eastwood Police, the one way our kind can truly die, though saying it aloud made it real in a way I wasn't ready for.

I told Adrian Keaton she protects me from boredom and loneliness, that she gives me a reason to stay undead—each word true, though I softened it with kisses to keep her from seeing how much I meant it.
I told her to go in—it was late—and made myself say I wouldn’t be coming back, not tonight, even though her face made it harder than anything I’ve endured.
She asked for one last kiss on her birthday, and I gave in—started gentle, but couldn’t control it, the urgency took over, like it was already goodbye.

I stood by her house, watching her climb out of the the black radio, relief on her face—until she saw mine. I asked her to walk with me and took her hand, feeling the dread in her stillness as I led her toward Northbridge Plaza.
I ran as hard as I could toward the edge, the wind tearing at me, and leapt—freezing midair—but the pain followed, unrelenting, even in the fall.
I saw her coming toward me, and I stepped back—then forced myself to retreat further, until the shadows swallowed me whole.
I appeared beside her as she moved forward, then again on her left, then ahead at the curve—each time willing her to see me, to react, though I knew I wasn't really there.
I was there, standing in the cold, watching her search—then my face wasn't mine anymore, it twisted into Noel Calloway's, and she reached for me just as I pulled away.

I yanked her back and pushed her out the door—she couldn’t stay, not with them looking at her like that, not with the danger still hanging in the air. The slam of the door was final, and I couldn’t let myself look back.
I appeared beside her when she stepped to the edge—her eyes lit up, but the moment she pulled back, I vanished. She knew exactly what would bring me back.
She started taking off her coat, and I reappeared—urgency in my voice as I told her to stop. But she didn't hesitate, not even when she looked at me one last time before jumping.
I reached for her as she sank, my hand nearly brushing hers—her eyes wide, searching mine—before something pulled me away, and the darkness took her.
I didn't want Taylor Brooks coming here, didn't want her interfering, but I couldn't stop her — and now Adrian Keaton knows I've been shutting her out, that I've been gone.
I remember the way the room tilted when Shawn Davenport said Adrian Keaton was dead—her voice breaking through my resolve like glass, and the word 'cliff' tearing something loose inside me.
I stared at the the wooden key, feeling everything break inside me, and then I threw it against the wall as hard as I could, watching it shatter.
I walked down that long corridor, knowing each step brought me closer to the doors—and to them. The weight of what I was about to do pressed on me, but I didn’t slow.
I asked if they had decided, and when they refused to end me, I knew I would have to force their hand—I would give them cause to destroy me.
I felt the sunlight just at my shoe, ready to end it, when Adrian Keaton crashed into me—solid, real—calling my name like a lifeline I no longer believed in.
I stared at her, stunned, the final chime echoing—her voice pulling me back from the edge, and in that moment, I knew I had to protect her, even from what I had become.
I took hold of Adrian Keaton's wrists and lowered her over the edge, feeling her weight in my hands as she dangled above the darkness.

I saw Logan Winslow turn toward Adrian Keaton, and I moved without thinking — placing myself between her and that cold, sadistic gaze. The moment her eyes locked on me, the pain tore through every nerve, but I didn't make a sound.

I felt Shawn Dalton probing the edge of my thoughts, and I saw what he intended — to have Logan Winslow test Adrian Keaton next. I shouted 'No!' before he could act, knowing I couldn't bear to see her suffer that torment.
Taylor Brooks was at my side quickly, her hand under my arm to pull me up — I could feel Adrian Keaton rushing to me too, close and warm, but I couldn't steady myself without their help.
I took hold of Adrian Keaton's arm, my grip firm — we moved backward toward the doors together, step by step, not turning away from them, not trusting it was over.

I saw Bennett Hart lead a group of tourists past us, ordinary people with cameras, and when Logan Foster whispered 'Nice fishing, Bennett Hart, save some for me,' I knew they weren't just visitors—they were prey.
I heard the screams start the moment the doors closed behind the last tourist—Adrian Keaton was looking back, and I pulled her forward, but the sound told me everything I needed to know.
I told her the truth—why I left wasn't because I didn't want her, but because I wanted her to have a normal life, one where she wouldn't be in constant danger because of me.
I asked if she could forgive me, knowing I didn't deserve it, and admitted I don't know how to live without her—then she melted, and I finally kissed her.
I asked her to wait three years as a human before I’d change her—just a compromise to hold on to her soul a little longer, though I knew the Eastwood Police wouldn’t make it that simple.
I slammed the brakes when I saw Noel Calloway standing in the road—he was staring right at me, defiant—then he just turned and walked away into the trees without a word.

dialogue_exemplars: We don't make spectacles of ourselves, nor kill conspicuously, unless we want to die.
Don't worry. You're human. Time heals all wounds for your kind. Particularly if you're not reminded.
Not the girl - the suicide. (off her look) Nearly impossible for my kind. But humans, a little poison, dagger to the heart. There are so many options.
"Friends" don't spend two weeks looking for the perfect dreamcatcher.
There are... ways for us. At least one way. I would have gone to Italy, provoked the Eastwood Police...
I had to be convincing. But easy? In my hundred years, I've never had a harder time than what I just went through.
You... think I asked the Eastwood Police to kill me because I felt guilty?
You got a paper cut. Normal people get paper cuts. And a normal boyfriend wouldn't have flung you into a stack of plates. A normal boyfriend wouldn't have had to fight the urge to kill you --
But I'm back now. And I'm not leaving Adrian Keaton's side till she orders me away.
I don't have that particular gift. But I can read a watch. I'm clever that way.
Try to understand. Every second with you is about restraint. You're too fragile. I'm tired of pretending to be something I'm not. Reining myself
Come on, the last real birthday any of us had was Lane Bennett's - I think Bing Crosby was on top of the charts.

Certainly not. But I apologize for being a distraction. Perhaps you should rewind to act five, scene one, line twenty-eight eighty-nine -- "If you had the strength of twenty men it would dispatch you straight."

memories.memory_text: I hugged Adrian Keaton when she got out of the the black radio—she seemed surprised, but I couldn’t help it. It was good to see her again, and that grin on my face just came naturally.

After she showed me those rusted bikes and talked about using her college fund, I called it stupid and reckless—but I leaned in and asked, 'When do we start?' I could see the spark in her eyes, and I knew we were doing this.
I was showing Adrian Keaton the the old box parts when Valerie Whitaker called out — my heart jumped, and I saw Adrian Keaton start to cover everything up, like we were being caught.

After the teasing about Adrian Keaton and me being more than friends, I laughed it off and things got loose — Valerie Whitaker went after me, Bennett Arden bet on the fight, and Adrian Keaton jumped in on the bet too, smiling like she belonged.
I pretended to stab myself with a pipe, just to make her laugh — it worked, and for a second, everything felt light again.
I kept touching her — brushing her arm, leaning in — not thinking, just doing, like it was natural, like I couldn't help it.

I was showing Adrian Keaton the crankshaft we pulled from the dump, joking about crankshaft-dot-com, and trying to get her excited about the bikes we’re fixing—then she mentioned a sunny place, and I saw her freeze up, remembering Avery Hale. I gave her my easiest smile and said, 'So we'll find our sunny spot, right?'—just to pull her back.

I couldn't hide how much it stung seeing Bennett Arden like that—shaved head, bulked up, just another one of Emery Winslow's followers. He used to joke about them being hall monitors on steroids, and now he's one of them.

I let that bitterness slip when I called them 'Emery Winslow and his disciples'—Adrian Keaton noticed. I don't like how they act like they own the place, like they're some kind of protectors, but saying it out loud made me feel exposed.
I felt her head, checking for injuries after the the old box fell on her—my hands were steady but my heart wasn’t, not with her looking up at me like that, dazed and determined.

I watched her ride forward, trying to stay calm, but every time that ghost of Avery Hale showed up beside her, I clenched my jaw—knowing he was the real danger, not me, and that she still chose to keep going.
I can't call her, no matter how much she wants me to — I'm barely holding it together, and if I hear her voice, I might lose control completely.

I told Adrian Keaton I was out with friends when she came by, but I couldn’t let her see me—she already knew the mono story didn’t add up, and I could hear the confusion in her voice when she asked about it.
I saw the shock in her eyes when she looked at me—no easy grin, no long hair, just the weight of what I’ve become pressing down in that stare.
I told her I can't be friends with her anymore—her voice cracked when she said she couldn't lose me too, but I had to make her understand it was over.
I called the Silverline Council 'filthy, reeking bloodsuckers'—my body was shaking, and I could feel the anger burning through me when she tried to pretend they weren't the reason everything changed.
I scratched at Riverside Plaza, my fingers catching on the frame—damn, that hurt—and hissed at her to open up; I needed to see her, now.

I had to make her remember the story about the Cold Ones on her own — I couldn’t say it outright, but I pushed her, desperate, asking if the myth was really just a myth, watching her eyes as it started to click.
I pulled her into a hug — her cheek against my chest — I didn’t want to go, but I had to. I felt her there, close, one last time before slipping out into the night.

I stepped in front of Adrian Keaton, facing Nico York—he was coming at her, calling her names, and I couldn’t let that stand. The second I pushed him, I felt my body start to shake, but I didn’t care.
I remember diving forward, the tear of skin and cloth as fur ripped through—then landing on all fours, the world sharper, louder. The only thing I saw was Nico York as a wolf, and I charged.
I told Adrian Keaton the truth — we don't kill innocent people, we kill vampires. When she finally understood, I saw the shock on her face, the way she reeled back like it was too much to take in.
I threw the fork at Emery Monroe—fast and hard—because he called Adrian Keaton bait, and I couldn't let that stand.
I told the others to back off when they kept pressing her, and when I saw how hurt she looked, I couldn't help but give her that look—like I was sorry they were doing this to her.
I told Adrian Keaton we've got the place covered and that she and Tristan Hayes are safe. I saw she looked blue, so I tried to cheer her up by suggesting cliff diving.
I suggested cliff diving to shake off the tension—I saw she needed a rush, something real. She said she could use it, and I promised we’d go soon, after we catch her.

I remember the impact—my body slamming into Quinn Colter, the force of it knocking her off Drew Huxley just as she was about to bite. The world narrowed to her red hair whipping through the air and the scent of rain and fear.
I hit Adrian Keaton’s back until she spat up water and finally looked at me, dazed, whispering my name — I couldn’t tell if she was scared or just confused.

After Emery Winslow told me to take her home, I told Adrian Keaton about Drew Huxley’s heart attack — she asked if her Tristan Hayes knew, and I said both our dads were already at the hospital, but I didn’t know if Drew Huxley would make it.
I told her I wasn't letting her go, but she said she didn't belong to me — those words cut deep, like I wasn't protecting her, just trapping her.
I handed her the keys and said 'Bye, Adrian Keaton, I hope you don't die' — I meant it, but it came out bitter, and she flinched like I'd struck her.

I broke my promise again—I saw the hurt in her eyes and couldn't walk away. I touched her face, remembering how simple things used to be, and leaned in, just wanting one moment before everything changed.

The the wooden key rang—right as I reached for her—and I answered without looking away. Then I heard 'funeral' and everything froze; my voice turned cold, and I felt the warmth between us shatter like it was never there.
I grabbed her arm, not to stop her — just to make her see me, to make her feel how much I was breaking. I said, 'Please, Adrian Keaton. Stay here. For Tristan Hayes... for me.'
I stood in the road to stop the car. I needed to talk to Avery Hale.

I saw them walking through the trees, and the way she looked at him—like he was the only thing that mattered. I had to say it first: 'You're still alive.' Couldn't let him think he just slips back in like nothing happened.

He stood there, thanking me like he deserved it—like coming back was some gift. And when he said he wouldn’t leave her side unless she told him to, I saw it in her eyes. She never would. 'We'll see,' I said, but I already knew.

Stay the hell out of my head!

Lying to Tristan Hayes. Blowing through college money. Repairing dangerous machines - that I'm guessing you'll want to ride?

Forget it. I'm revoking your the old box privileges.
Man, I thought maybe you wouldn't be such a hypocrite -- what, I'm not the right kind of monster for you? Can't measure up to your bloodsucking friends --

Then why are you taking Adrian Keaton to them
like a bottle of wine to a party?
Scrap metal. You shouldn't have.
Oh it's totally stupid and reckless. (leans closer, grins) When do we start?
If any of them bites a human, the truce is over. That's bite, not kill.
It's not a life-style choice. It's in my DNA.
